findings.obligation: ADR-NAV-POLISH-007: the floor is a reading, anchored on .lane-menu-trigger, and it goes red the moment the exemption widens past the rail. Risk Y8: an exemption that reads a fill, a tag or a class instead of rail membership must stay caught.
findings.observation: The floor asserts only that the list is not empty, so it catches a total emptying and nothing smaller. Keyed again on a quiet fill - the widening Y8 names - the opaque lane trigger, whose fill is var(--cz-surface), stays read and the floor stays green while every transparent control outside the rail leaves the reading unseen. The ADR anchor is also unchecked by name: if production moved the lane-actions trigger inside the rail or stopped rendering a column, other outside-rail controls would keep the list non-empty and the law would quietly lose the anchor the ADR says it owes a replacement for. The predicate is the only skip in the loop, so the floor can be computed from a fact the predicate cannot hide.
findings.remediation: Anchor the floor on the probe fact instead of on the predicate under test: assert that every control the walk reports with inTheNav false appears among the controls read, which fails on ANY widening, not only a total one. Alternatively, or additionally, assert the ADR anchor by name - that a control matching .lane-menu-trigger was among those read - with the recorded modal-close fallback named in the message.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs, assert_no_word_is_drawn_by_sign_out, the find_all count of svg.sidebar__icon
findings.obligation: A reading claims no observation it does not make. The message states that a member which draws neither a word nor a glyph is one the operator cannot use at all, so the guard has to read a glyph she can see.
findings.observation: find_all returns an element whether or not it is painted, so the guard reads DOM presence and not a drawn glyph. The open desk layout hides the very same element with display none, which is a presentation one stylesheet edit away, so a phone bar that clipped its word AND hid its glyph would leave this row green over a member showing the operator nothing. The walk already owns the right predicate: drawn() in CONTROL_BOUNDARY_PROBE refuses a node with no client rect, display none, visibility hidden, opacity zero or a clip-path.
findings.remediation: Read the glyph as drawn rather than as present - a non-empty client rect with a computed display other than none, or the probe own drawn() predicate - or, if presence is all this row wants, word the message for presence and leave the drawn reading to the phone row of the nav lane.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature, the scenario title On her phone the nav one control owes no outline, and shows no word to read
findings.obligation: A scenario title states truthfully what the operator meets and what the row requires.
findings.observation: The title says one control, and the row requires two: its first Then runs assert_the_rail_controls_owe_no_boundary, which fails unless a control naming Sign out AND a control naming theme-toggle are both found inside the rail. My run shows both are really there at 390 px - the step passed - and the phone block of the stylesheet sizes .theme-toggle beside .sidebar__item, so the bar carries two controls. The reading is right and the title undercounts it, which is the kind of mismatch that sends a later reader looking for a second control the row already covers.
findings.remediation: Name both controls in the title, for example that the two controls of the bar owe no outline and show no word to read, or narrow the first Then to the single control the title names.

observations.text: DELTA SELECTION, mechanical, round three. argv: git diff --stat e9ebe92..HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance, exit 0: four files, 369 insertions, 75 deletions - src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs (+375/-75 by stat), tests/features/canzan-theme-system.feature (+54/-6), src/support/rail_reading.rs (+7/-4), src/steps/feature_ui_nav_polish.rs (+3/-1). argv: git status --porcelain, exit 0, empty, so the judged bytes are the bytes of 421c669 and no approved byte is dirty. argv: git diff --numstat plus a comment-line filter over the last two files, exit 0: 15 changed lines, every one a // or //! comment line, and zero changed non-comment lines. Those two files therefore change no reading, so the ui-nav-polish and nav-collapse-icon-rail lanes are not affected and are not rerun; their measured runs stand from the delta-two round at commit 89f73c16 (ui-nav-polish 28 of 30 with the two word rows red at that production, nav-collapse-icon-rail 17 of 17, exit 0). The one affected lane is us-cts-01.

THE AFFECTED LANE RUNS GREEN, my own run. argv: scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=us-cts-01 timeout --kill-after=60 2400 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance", exit 0, host exit 0. Summary: 1 feature, 10 scenarios, 10 passed; 81 steps, 81 passed, no failure and no skip with fail_on_skipped on. Both new rows ran every step. With the nav narrowed its two controls owe no outline: the narrow-and-stop stimulus, no rail control asked for a fill or an outline, a control outside the nav still read at 3 to 1, the revealed word legible at 4.5 to 1, and the same four readings again in the light palette. On her phone the nav one control owes no outline: the phone board in the dark palette, the same two boundary readings, no ratio read for a wordless rail control, and the same three again in the light palette. Production is 54d315f, so green is the expected state for this round and no row is owed RED.

THE FLOOR CAN FAIL, and where it cannot. The boundary walk skips a control only through inside_the_rail, which reads the probe fact inTheNav, that is el.closest(.sidebar), and nothing else; every other control is measured and its name pushed into read_outside, and the row then refuses an empty read_outside. A widening keyed on containment - exempting the whole shell, or any ancestor above the rail - empties that list and the row goes red with a message that names the cause. The list is non-empty today for a real reason: the lane-actions trigger of every board column is button.lane-menu-trigger in partials/board_columns.html:44, outside the rail aside, carried in the walk node list because it is a plain button inside .app-shell, and it declares border 1px var(--cz-muted) over var(--cz-surface), measured in the stylesheet comment at 5.52 to 1 light and 6.08 to 1 dark. So the floor member is a true negative that MEETS 3 to 1 rather than a control the law must forgive, which is what ADR-NAV-POLISH-007 decided. The limit is recorded as a finding: non-emptiness is weaker than the risk the ADR names.

THE EXEMPTION CANNOT REACH A CONTROL OUTSIDE THE RAIL. inside_the_rail is one line over the probe containment fact, so no fill, class, tag, glyph or drawn word can move a control into the exempt set. The word reading is doubly fenced: assert_rail_words_are_legible skips a control that is not inside the rail AND a control whose word is empty, so an outside control can never take the word reading in place of the boundary reading, and a rail control with no drawn word is measured for nothing instead of being measured against a clipped sliver. The exempt set is load-bearing rather than free: assert_the_rail_controls_owe_no_boundary first requires that a control naming Sign out and a control naming theme-toggle are both found INSIDE the rail - so a theme control that a script mounted outside it would fail the row rather than pass unnoticed - and then requires that the quietest rail control computes BELOW 3 to 1, so a green row means the exemption did the work and not an outline the control happens to carry. Both requirements passed in all three layouts and both palettes in my run.

THE PHONE ROW AND A MEMBER THAT SHOWS NOTHING. The row asks for no ratio where no word is drawn, and it is guarded on both sides. First, assert_rail_words_are_legible is called with no owed word and returns the words it read, and the row refuses the word Sign out among them, so a bar that still laid the desk nav out would fail instead of passing silently. Second, the row then requires exactly one glyph element inside the sign-out submit, so a member that carried neither a word nor a glyph fails. The guard stops short of what its message claims, which is recorded as a finding: the glyph is counted by element presence through find_all, not read as drawn, and a regression that hid it the way the open desk layout does would keep the row green. Within that limit the answer to the question asked is that the row cannot pass on a member with no glyph at all, and can pass on a member whose glyph element is present but not painted.

THE TWO OPEN FINDINGS OF ROUND TWO ARE CLOSED. The design finding on the geometry scope of the control-boundary exemption is resolved by ADR-NAV-POLISH-006 and -007 at db338e7, which key the exemption on rail membership in every layout, and by the two new rows that now read the narrowed nav and the phone bar in both palettes - the two geometries whose scope and result were unobserved when I raised it. The oracle finding on the clip-versus-cover claim is corrected in the bytes: rail_reading.rs now states that the answer does NOT tell the two causes apart, that it is reported as evidence rather than diagnosis, and that whoever reads it still has to look at the rail overflow and its paint level; the module header of feature_ui_nav_polish.rs carries the same correction. Both are what the findings asked for. diagnostic: ACCEPTED, round three at 421c669 with a clean tree. The delta moves the WCAG 1.4.11 exemption from a drawn word to rail containment, as ADR-NAV-POLISH-006 and -007 decided, and it closes the two findings that were open: the design finding on the geometry scope of the exemption, now settled for every layout and read in the narrowed nav and on the phone in both palettes, and my oracle finding on the clip-versus-cover claim, now reworded in both files to report evidence rather than diagnosis. The three questions asked are answered. The floor CAN fail: the walk skips a control only through the containment predicate, so a widening keyed on containment empties the outside-rail reading and the row goes red; the floor has a real member today, button.lane-menu-trigger, outside the rail, read, and meeting 3 to 1 at 5.52 light and 6.08 dark, which is a true negative and not a forgiven control. The exemption CANNOT pass a control outside the rail: the predicate is one line over the probe containment fact, the word reading additionally skips an empty word, and the exempt set is load-bearing because the row first requires Sign out and the theme control to be found inside the rail and then requires the quietest rail control to be below 3 to 1. The phone row cannot pass on a member with no glyph at all, and the word guard refuses the word Sign out among those read. Measured: us-cts-01 10 of 10 scenarios, 81 of 81 steps, exit 0, both new rows running every step in both palettes; the other two lanes are not rerun because the only changes in their files are 15 comment lines and zero non-comment lines, with the delta-two runs cited for them. Three findings stay open, none blocking: the floor asserts non-emptiness rather than the ADR anchor or the raw containment fact, so a partial widening keyed on a quiet fill stays green; the phone glyph guard counts an element rather than a drawn glyph, which its own message overstates; and the phone scenario title says one control where the row requires two. Limit: typesafe unavailable, so every judgment here is local and reviewer-owned.
